summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with hands-on robotics software experience spanning ROS2, forward kinematics, and simulation environments including CARLA and ABB RobotStudio. Built and validated simulated robot behavior against physical hardware, from URDF-modeled kinematic chains to closed-loop pick-and-place trajectories. Proficient in C++ and Python across simulation, perception, and embedded control pipelines.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Organized 10+ exhibitions and technical workshops covering Arduino, PCB design, and SolidWorks.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and hand-computed full forward kinematic chains (0T6) for a 6-DoF UR5e and a 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on physical UR5e via UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability measured at under 2mm over 10 trials.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Built automated synthetic data generation pipelines in CARLA using semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering to produce thousands of YOLO and lane-detection training frames with zero manual annotation.

Trained and fine-tuned perception models integrated into an adaptive control stack with lane-following and waypoint fallback; validated across multi-agent traffic scenarios with zero collisions and correct traffic light compliance.

projects.name: ABB RobotStudio Automation Simulation
bullets: Designed and simulated a full ABB RobotStudio workcell for an end-to-end press-to-packing assembly pipeline including CAD-modeled fixtures, validating digital twin behavior against real cycle timing.
Programmed in RAPID with TCP socket-based pose acquisition and interrupt-driven press-bench logic; validated full-cycle repeatability.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system bridging simulated planning and physical robot behavior across a Jetson and Arduino controller pipeline in C++ and Python.
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO visual servoing (5.2x speedup) and dual ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping; resolved 11 integration failures to reach 100% pick reliability across trials.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection.
